content.text:
I rewrote `/private/tmp/gndfv/0.svg`. It was a 41-byte empty root element that rendered nothing and had no size, so it would collapse to zero or default dimensions in most viewers. The new file is a complete, scalable, accessible SVG.

Because the original had no content, I had to choose what it should show. I took the filename as the cue and drew the numeral zero as a stroked ellipse. If you meant a different image, tell me what it should depict and I'll redo the artwork while keeping the structure.

The new file:

```svg
<?xml version="1.0" encoding="UTF-8"?>
<svg xmlns="http://www.w3.org/2000/svg" width="64" height="64" viewBox="0 0 64 64" role="img" aria-labelledby="title">
  <title id="title">Zero</title>
  <ellipse cx="32" cy="32" rx="15" ry="21" fill="none" stroke="#111111" stroke-width="7"/>
</svg>
```

What changed and why:

- **Added a viewBox plus width and height.** The graphic now has a fixed 64 by 64 intrinsic size and scales cleanly to any display size without distortion.
- **Added a role and a title.** Screen readers announce it as an image named "Zero" instead of skipping it or reading nothing.
- **Added visible content.** A single ellipse with a 7-unit stroke, centered with even margins, is easy to recolor or reshape by editing one line.
- **Added an XML declaration.** This is standard for a standalone SVG file and states the encoding explicitly.

One caveat. Every verification command was auto-denied by this session's permission settings, which have no approval surface. That blocked the XML well-formedness check, the Quick Look and librsvg renders, the tool availability check, and the extended-attribute lookup I wanted for context on the file's origin. I verified the markup by inspection only: it is a single properly closed root with quoted attributes, and the ellipse's outer edge stays inside the viewBox on every side. Opening the file in a browser will confirm the render.
